# Import fixtures

These files exercise PLUME's mesh import path. They are generated by PLUME's own
exporter, not downloaded or copied from another project.

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `import-cube.obj` + `.mtl` | OBJ geometry and material import |
| `import-cube.glb` | Binary glTF import |
| `import-cube.stl` | Binary STL import |

Each file contains a small unit cube built by
[`core/examples/generate_samples.rs`](../core/examples/generate_samples.rs) and
written through the corresponding exporter. The cube uses PLUME coordinates
(Y up), includes guide geometry, and is deliberately simple so import failures
are easy to diagnose.

## Regeneration

```bash
cargo run -p plume-core --example generate_samples
```

The generator also rewrites the samples under `../samples/`.

## Using the fixtures

Open one from the studio with **File → Open**, or pass it on the command line:

```bash
PLUME_SANDBOX="$PWD" cargo run -p plume-app -- \
  --file testdata/import-cube.obj \
  --render docs/renders/import-cube.png
```

The imported result is an editable document whose geometry is stored as an
imported mesh guide. It is not a native curve scene until you draw on it.
